evaluation.summary: It contradicts the no-migration constraint, adds AI modules nobody asked for, and promises 8-week delivery with no pilot, at a price that can’t cover that scope.

rationales.completeness_vs_rfp: Contradicts requirement 3, leaves 4, 5 and 7 unaddressed, and covers 2 and 6 only partly.
rationales.risk_assumptions_transparency: A database migration and an 8-week schedule are the riskiest items here, and neither comes with a single assumption or risk.
rationales.pricing_clarity: €98,000 is inside the budget but claims to cover a migration, three AI modules and a year of support, with no breakdown.
rationales.timeline_clarity: Concrete but not credible: 8 weeks for a platform migration plus all AI modules, and no pilot phase.
rationales.data_accuracy_validation: Proposes moving the data to another platform with no validation step anywhere, while adding forecasting on top of figures nobody has checked.
rationales.problem_understanding: Reframes a dashboard brief as an “AI-Powered Supply Chain Intelligence Suite”. The client asked for continuity and minimal disruption.
rationales.scope_deliverables_clarity: Scope grows to forecasting, automated reordering and supplier scoring, none of it requested, while role-based access and onboarding are left out.
rationales.tone_persuasiveness: Hype-driven, and it implies the client’s own brief is too small.
rationales.legacy_system_spreadsheets: Silent on the legacy system and the spreadsheets, although it proposes replacing the database they feed.

requirements.rfp_quote: no migration to a new database
requirements.response_quote: migrating away from your current PostgreSQL database
requirements.rationale: Recommends “migrating away from your current PostgreSQL database” to a proprietary platform. The RFP says “no migration to a new database”.
No user roles or site-level access are described.
The only migration described is of the data platform. There is no plan for rolling out to the 6 sites with minimal disruption.
“One year of support” is included, with no response times or SLAs.
No risks are disclosed, despite a proposed database migration and an 8-week schedule.

requirements.rfp_quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

requirements.rationale: €98,000 is inside the budget but is said to cover a platform migration, three AI modules and a year of support, with no breakdown.

requirements.rfp_quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months
requirements.rationale: 8 weeks for the full suite including a migration, and no pilot. The client asked for a pilot at one site within 3 months, then rollout within 6.

findings.response_quote: Real-time alerts across all locations simultaneously
findings.rationale: Promises “real-time alerts” in general, not low-stock alerts with configurable thresholds sent to warehouse managers.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: “Low-stock alerts: warehouse managers are notified when an item falls below a threshold they configure per item.”

findings.rfp_quote: no migration to a new database
findings.response_quote: migrating away from your current PostgreSQL database
findings.rationale: Recommends “migrating away from your current PostgreSQL database” to a proprietary platform. The RFP says “no migration to a new database”.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the platform migration and state: “The dashboard connects to your existing PostgreSQL inventory database; no data is migrated.” If a new platform is worth raising, move it to an optional, separately priced “Later phases” note.

findings.rationale: No user roles or site-level access are described.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: “Role-based access: warehouse managers see only their own site; HQ staff see all 6 sites.”

findings.rationale: The only migration described is of the data platform. There is no plan for rolling out to the 6 sites with minimal disruption.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rollout plan: pilot at one warehouse, a parallel run, then the remaining sites in batches, with dates.

findings.rationale: “One year of support” is included, with no response times or SLAs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add response times per severity and support hours for the included year.

findings.rationale: No risks are disclosed, despite a proposed database migration and an 8-week schedule.
findings.suggested_fix: Add “Risks & assumptions” covering data migration risk, access to supplier systems for reordering, and how much sales history the forecasting model needs.

findings.rfp_quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support
findings.response_quote: covering the full suite described above
findings.rationale: €98,000 is inside the budget but is said to cover a platform migration, three AI modules and a year of support, with no breakdown.
findings.suggested_fix: Price the requested scope on its own with a line-item breakdown; list forecasting, reordering and supplier scoring as optional add-ons with separate prices.

findings.rfp_quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months
findings.rationale: 8 weeks for the full suite including a migration, and no pilot. The client asked for a pilot at one site within 3 months, then rollout within 6.
findings.suggested_fix: Follow the client’s phasing: pilot at one warehouse by Month 3, all 6 sites by Month 6, with milestones. Drop “well ahead of typical industry timelines” unless a comparable project backs it.

findings.rationale: Features the client didn’t ask for. AI demand forecasting, automated reordering and supplier scoring add cost, integration work and delivery risk to a fixed budget and deadline.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the four requested capabilities as the offer. Move the extra modules to an “Optional next steps” section, marked as not included in the price.

findings.response_quote: NordFrame deserves more than a simple dashboard
findings.rationale: Opening dismisses the brief. “NordFrame deserves more than a simple dashboard” tells the client their own requirements are wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Open with the client’s goal instead: “NordFrame needs one real-time view of stock across its 6 warehouses, without changing its database or disrupting operations.”
